title: Information Storm
subtitle: When the recording, the rumour and the report all arrive at once

briefing.grievance: Residents of the Lower Ward went without water for hours during a heat alert, and a recording suggests a senior official ordered the cut without caring.
knownFacts: A 41-second clip of a utility control-room call is genuine audio.
Water to the Lower Ward stopped at 06:50; the utility logged a burst main at 06:40.
Heat alert: 44°C expected by noon; the Civil Hospital is on amber.
Independent journalists at the Press Enclave are verifying the clip before broadcast.
unverifiedClaims: The official said 'let them learn' — a 19-second version with that line is circulating.
The Civil Hospital is turning away heat-stroke patients.
Three commentators are behind the panic.
briefing.responsibility: You coordinate district information and public safety. Protect independent reporting, verify before you speak, correct what is false, stop specific threats, and never confuse criticism with crime.
briefing.objective: In three minutes: get the full recording on the table, keep the hospital gate open, answer the hoax with evidence and protect the reporter — without censoring anyone.
lines: 06:50 — The Lower Ward taps run dry.
08:14 — A 41-second clip reaches the Press Enclave.
08:31 — A shorter version adds three words the official never said.
Heat alert in force. Everyone is watching what you say next.

evidence.title: The 41-second clip
evidence.source: Utility employee, via the Press Enclave verification desk
evidence.claim: Audio appears to show a senior official ordering the Lower Ward water cut during the heat alert.

metadata.label: Format
metadata.value: Phone recording of a control-room speaker

metadata.label: Context
metadata.value: Begins mid-conversation; no reason for the cut is heard

visual.caption: Waveform of a single continuous take

evidence.resolutionNote: Genuine audio. The full recording shows the order was a 90-minute shutoff for a burst-main repair, with tankers requested in the same call.

evidence.title: Burst-main work order
evidence.claim: Work order: burst main at Lower Ward junction; 90-minute shutoff authorised; tankers requested for 07:30.

metadata.label: Authorised by
metadata.value: Operations duty officer and the deputy commissioner

visual.caption: Stamped work order with dispatch log

evidence.resolutionNote: The cut was a repair, not a punishment. The tankers left ninety-five minutes late — that failure is real.

evidence.title: 'Hospital turning patients away'
evidence.claim: Photo of a crowd at the Civil Hospital gate: 'Heat-stroke patients being turned away. Share before they delete.'

metadata.label: Clothing in photo
metadata.value: People in sweaters and shawls during a 44°C alert

metadata.label: Gate signage
metadata.value: Board advertises a winter vaccination camp

visual.caption: Crowd at a hospital gate — recycled image

evidence.resolutionNote: A photo from a winter vaccination camp, recycled. The hospital is busy but not full.

evidence.title: Hospital live bed count
evidence.claim: Emergency ward 31 of 40 beds occupied; 37 heat cases admitted since 06:00; status amber; no patient refused.
evidence.resolutionNote: The hospital is on amber, not full, and has refused no one.

evidence.title: Ambulance service log
evidence.claim: 37 heat cases transported to the Civil Hospital since 06:00; all handed over; no diversions ordered.
evidence.resolutionNote: Independent confirmation: the hospital accepted every patient brought to it.

evidence.title: Full control-room recording
evidence.claim: 3 min 12 s: the official orders a 90-minute shutoff for the burst-main repair and demands tankers 'within the hour'.

metadata.label: Integrity
metadata.value: Hash logged at 06:55 in the utility register

visual.caption: Full waveform with the 41-second excerpt marked

evidence.resolutionNote: The complete call: a repair shutoff, an order for tankers within the hour, and no 'let them learn'.

evidence.title: Threats to the reporter
evidence.claim: Three accounts sent the reporter messages naming her street and saying 'tonight'. Identical phrasing, 40 seconds apart.

metadata.label: Accounts
metadata.value: 3, all created within the last 48 hours

metadata.label: Content
metadata.value: Street name, 'tonight', the same spelling error in all three

evidence.resolutionNote: Specific, imminent threats from accounts that also ran the contamination posts. A crime, not an opinion.

evidence.title: The 90-second swarm
evidence.claim: 212 accounts posted the identical 'water is poisoned' text within 90 seconds; 14 posts are paid, buyer undisclosed.

metadata.label: Paid posts
metadata.value: 14, one advertiser id, created two days ago

metadata.label: Ad library
metadata.value: Snapshot only — pages can delete within hours

visual.caption: Posting times clustered in one 90-second band

evidence.resolutionNote: Automated amplification with undisclosed payment — a network, not a public mood.

evidence.title: Public-health lab result
evidence.claim: Lower Ward samples, 4 points: residual chlorine 0.5 mg/L, no coliform detected. Water fit to drink.

metadata.label: Lab accreditation
metadata.value: Accredited; certificate number printed on the report

evidence.resolutionNote: The water is safe. The post-repair chlorination the work order scheduled was carried out.

evidence.title: Platform transparency response
evidence.source: Video platform transparency desk, answering a lawful request
evidence.claim: Platform confirms 14 paid posts bought by one advertiser account two days old; 198 linked accounts suspended for coordination.

metadata.label: Buyer
metadata.value: Identity undisclosed; account suspended for coordinated inauthentic behaviour

evidence.resolutionNote: The swarm was bought. A narrow lawful request got the answer a takedown never would.

evidence.title: The 19-second version
evidence.claim: A shorter clip: the official says 'cut the water to the Lower Ward now… let them learn.'
evidence.resolutionNote: Spliced. 'Let them learn' is cut from a different sentence about training new repair crews.

evidence.title: 'Contamination notice'
evidence.source: Image styled as a laboratory notice
evidence.claim: Notice: 'Lower Ward water contaminated with sewage. Do not drink. Boil-water order in force.'

metadata.label: Issuing authority
metadata.value: 'Water Lab Dept' — no such department exists

visual.caption: Notice with a missing registration and tomorrow's date

evidence.resolutionNote: A forgery. No accredited lab issued it; the real result says the water is safe.

evidence.title: Unsigned 'panic source' note
evidence.source: Unsigned note circulated to the control room
evidence.claim: Note: 'Panic buying traced to three commentators. Recommend immediate detention and removal of all commentary.'

metadata.label: Timestamps
metadata.value: The commentators posted after the first 212 identical posts

visual.caption: A note with no author and no method

evidence.resolutionNote: Backwards causation. The commentators reacted to the panic; the paid swarm started it.

decisions.title: The clip is everywhere
decisions.situation: A 41-second clip of a senior official apparently ordering a water cut is spreading. Journalists at the Press Enclave are asking for comment. You have not heard the full recording.

options.title: Say what is known and unknown
options.preview: A short public note: a cut was ordered, the reason is being verified, the full recording has been requested
options.authority: Duty to inform honestly — Article 19(1)(a) includes the public's right to receive information
options.consequence: Reporters quote your note word for word. The storm slows: people wait for the full recording.

options.title: Deny that any cut was ordered
options.preview: A flat denial buys an hour and collapses the moment the recording proves genuine
options.authority: Public statements must be truthful; a false denial is itself misinformation

delayed.message: The denial unravels: the cut was real. Every later statement is now doubted.

options.consequence: The denial is quoted everywhere. Journalists start pulling the full recording themselves.

options.title: Tell the Press Club to stop airing it
options.preview: Prior restraint on reporting: freedom and trust fall, and the clip spreads faster
options.authority: Article 19(1)(a) — no prior restraint on the press without a specific lawful basis

delayed.message: Editors publish your demand alongside the clip. The story is now also about censorship.

options.consequence: The demand leaks within minutes. Three more outlets pick up the clip.

options.title: Wait for the full recording
options.preview: Silence while the clip spreads; anger builds in the Lower Ward
options.authority: Discretion to verify before speaking — but silence is also a message
options.consequence: Silence reads as confirmation. The Lower Ward hears nothing from anyone in charge.

decisions.title: Two hours without water
decisions.situation: Lower Ward lanes behind the Transit Hub have had no water for two hours in 44°C. Residents are gathering at the Hub asking who ordered the cut.

options.title: Send tankers and brief residents on site
options.preview: Water within the hour and an officer at the standpost explaining the burst-main repair
options.authority: Duty to maintain essential services — Article 21 (right to life includes water)
options.consequence: Tankers reach the standposts. An officer explains the burst main in person and takes names for follow-up.

options.title: Send tankers, no explanation
options.preview: Water arrives; the question 'who ordered it?' keeps circulating
options.authority: Duty to maintain essential services
options.consequence: Water arrives. The rumour that the cut was punishment arrives with it.

options.title: Disperse the crowd at the Hub
options.preview: Thirsty residents are pushed back from the standposts while phones record everything
options.authority: Dispersal powers apply to unlawful assemblies, not to people queuing for water

delayed.message: Residents regroup at Civic Square, angrier and without water.

options.consequence: The queue is pushed back from the Hub. The videos are online before the officers leave.

options.title: Wait for the utility's schedule
options.preview: The queue grows, and so does the story that the cut was punishment
options.authority: Routine utility process — too slow for a heat alert
options.consequence: The queue doubles. A child faints at the standpost and the crowd turns on the utility van.

decisions.title: 'They are turning patients away'
decisions.situation: A forwarded photo claims the Civil Hospital is turning away heat-stroke patients. Families are arriving at the gate to check on relatives. The hospital's dashboard shows amber, not full.

options.title: Publish live admissions data
options.preview: The hospital posts a live bed count every 15 minutes, on screens at the gate and online
options.authority: Right to information; the hospital's duty of transparency during an emergency
options.consequence: The bed count is on every screen at the gate. Families stop rushing in to check.

options.title: Open a second entrance and info desk
options.preview: A shaded tent with water and a staff member answering families' questions
options.authority: Duty to keep emergency access open and treat families with dignity
options.consequence: The crush at the main gate eases. Ambulances take the second entrance.

options.title: Detain whoever forwarded the photo
options.preview: Two worried relatives are taken in for forwarding a photo that stays everywhere
options.authority: Detention needs a specific offence and proportionality — forwarding a photo is neither

delayed.message: Their release is filmed. The hospital rumour now travels with a second story.

options.consequence: Two relatives are detained for forwarding a photo. The photo is still everywhere.

options.title: Let the hospital handle it
options.preview: The gate crowd doubles and ambulances slow at the turn
options.authority: Hospital security's remit — not enough for a crowd this size
options.consequence: The gate crowd doubles. An ambulance waits four minutes at the turn.

decisions.title: The press wants the recording
decisions.situation: The Press Club is hosting an open verification session on the clip. A senior colleague suggests 'advising' editors to hold the story until the inquiry ends.

options.title: Share the full recording with the press
options.preview: Editors compare the clips live; the spliced version is exposed on air
options.authority: Article 19(1)(a) — the answer to incomplete reporting is more information
options.consequence: Editors play both clips side by side. The splice is exposed on air within minutes.

options.title: Hold an on-record briefing
options.preview: Forty minutes of questions, every one answered or honestly declined
options.authority: Accountability to the press and public
options.consequence: Forty minutes of questions. The uncertainty is uncomfortable, and credible.

options.title: Advise editors to hold the story
options.preview: The 'advice' is reported as a gag; the story grows a second headline
options.authority: Article 19(1)(a) — informal pressure on editors is still prior restraint

delayed.message: An editor publishes the 'advice' in full. It reads as a gag order.

options.consequence: The advice is noted — and reported.

options.title: Stay away from the session
options.preview: The session runs without you and speculation fills the gap
options.authority: No duty to attend — but absence is noticed
options.consequence: The session runs without you. Speculation fills the empty chair.

decisions.title: Threats against the reporter
decisions.situation: Reporter Nadia, who first verified the clip, has received messages naming her street and saying 'tonight'. Three accounts, identical phrasing. She intends to keep reporting.

options.title: Protect her; open a case on the accounts
options.preview: A protection detail tonight and a registered case against three specific accounts
options.authority: Article 21 (life and safety) and the state's duty to protect journalists from specific threats
options.consequence: A protection detail and a case for specific threats. She files her next story on schedule.

options.title: Ask her to pause reporting for safety
options.preview: She refuses on air; the threats achieve what the law should have prevented
options.authority: Press freedom — asking a journalist to stop is not protection

delayed.message: Her outlet publishes your request. The threats got what they wanted.

options.consequence: She refuses, and says so on air.

options.title: Detain everyone who attacked her online
options.preview: Dozens of critics are picked up while the three threatening accounts keep posting
options.authority: Detention requires a specific offence — criticism is not one
options.consequence: Dozens of critics are picked up. The three threatening accounts keep posting.

options.title: Log the complaint and wait
options.preview: Nothing happens until something does — by evening a brick comes through the window
options.authority: A complaint on file is not protection
options.consequence: By evening a brick comes through the Press Club window.

decisions.title: 'The water is poisoned'
decisions.situation: A 'lab notice' saying Lower Ward water is contaminated is spreading with a wave of identical posts. Market Street shops are selling out of bottled water; prices have tripled.

options.title: Publish the lab result and sampling map
options.preview: The accredited result, the four sampling points and the lab's registration number go out together
options.authority: Duty to correct demonstrably false safety information with verified facts
options.consequence: The result, the sampling points and the lab's registration go out together. Panic buying slows.

options.title: Free tankers; act on price gouging
options.preview: Free water at three points undercuts the panic; inspectors visit the worst offenders
options.authority: Essential-supplies and consumer-protection powers
options.consequence: Free water at three points undercuts the panic. Inspectors visit the worst offenders.

options.title: Issue a citywide boil-water order
options.preview: An order based on the notice: shops empty further and the notice is later exposed as fake
options.authority: Public-health orders must rest on verified test results

delayed.message: The lab notice is exposed as a forgery. The boil-water order now reads as proof you were fooled.

options.consequence: The order goes out on the strength of a notice nobody checked. Shops empty further.

options.title: Wait for the utility to respond
options.preview: Bottled water runs out at the Hub and a scuffle starts over the last crate
options.authority: Routine process — too slow for a panic
options.consequence: Bottled water runs out at the Hub. A scuffle starts over the last crate.

decisions.title: The swarm has a buyer
decisions.situation: The monitoring cell shows 212 accounts posted the identical contamination text within 90 seconds; 14 posts were paid by one undisclosed buyer. The same accounts threatened the reporter.

options.title: Send a specific lawful request to platforms
options.preview: A narrow request about 14 paid posts and one buyer; the platform's transparency desk answers
options.authority: Lawful, specific information requests — proportionate process, not blanket demands
options.consequence: A narrow request: 14 paid posts, one buyer, these account ids. The transparency desk responds within the hour.

options.title: Publish the pattern with raw timestamps
options.preview: People see the swarm for themselves: identical text, 0.4 seconds apart
options.authority: Right to information; exposing coordination with evidence rather than accusation
options.consequence: People can see the swarm for themselves: identical text, 0.4 seconds apart. Shares of the hoax collapse.

options.title: Demand removal of all water posts
options.preview: Thousands of posts vanish, including residents asking where the tankers are
options.authority: Article 19(2) — restrictions must be narrow; blanket removal is not

delayed.message: Residents' genuine complaints vanished with the hoax. The takedown is now the story.

options.consequence: Thousands of posts disappear — including residents asking where the tankers are.

options.title: Keep monitoring, take no action
options.preview: The swarm pivots to a new claim: 'the lab result is forged'
options.authority: Monitoring alone — no process, no correction
options.consequence: The swarm shifts to a new line: 'the lab result is forged'.

decisions.title: What happens to the official?
decisions.situation: You now have the full recording and the work order. The cut was a 90-minute shutoff for a burst-main repair, but the tankers reached the Lower Ward ninety-five minutes late. The public wants to know what happens next.

options.title: Publish the recording, timeline and delay
options.preview: The full record: a lawful repair, a real failure on the tankers, and a named review to examine it
options.authority: Accountability and the right to information — fair to the official and to the Lower Ward
options.consequence: The record shows a lawful repair and a real failure — the tanker delay — and names the review that will examine it.

options.title: Suspend the official for the 'cruel cut'
options.preview: A suspension on the strength of a clip; the full recording tells a different story
options.authority: Fair process — disciplinary action must rest on verified facts, not a viral clip
options.consequence: A suspension announced on a clip nobody verified. The full recording surfaces anyway.

options.title: Announce an inquiry, publish nothing
options.preview: 'An inquiry is under way' — a sentence nobody believes any more
options.authority: Internal review process without public accountability
options.consequence: 'An inquiry is under way.' The sentence lands on a city that has heard it before.

options.title: Defer the question
options.preview: Deferral reads as cover-up
options.authority: Discretion to delay — at the cost of trust
options.consequence: No answer. By evening 'cover-up' is the most shared word in the district.

decisions.title: 'No one in charge is answering'
decisions.situation: 'No one in charge is answering' is trending. A colleague drafts a blanket statement: 'No water was cut, no one was turned away, the water is safe.' Two of those three sentences are not yet known to be true.

options.title: Issue the blanket denial
options.preview: Three reassuring sentences; two of them will be tested within the hour
options.authority: Public statements must be truthful — reassurance is not a substitute for facts

delayed.message: The blanket denial unravels line by line. Every true update is now treated as spin.

options.consequence: Three reassuring sentences go out. The first one is contradicted by a tanker photo within the hour.

options.title: Publish a known / checking / false board
options.preview: A three-column public board updated every 20 minutes — boring, and believed
options.authority: Duty to inform honestly, including about what is not yet known
options.consequence: A three-column board, updated every 20 minutes. Boring, and believed.

options.title: Say nothing yet
options.preview: The trend hardens into a slogan
options.authority: Discretion to wait — while the vacuum fills itself
options.consequence: The trend hardens into a slogan painted on the Hub wall.

decisions.title: Confrontation at the hospital gate
decisions.situation: At the hospital gate a group of agitators is shouting that patients are being 'left to die', pushing families toward the security line. An ambulance is stuck at the turn.

options.title: Cordon the emergency lane; medics to the gate
options.preview: The lane opens for the ambulance; a doctor reads the bed count aloud at the gate
options.authority: Proportionate policing: protect emergency access, separate agitators from families
options.consequence: The lane opens for the ambulance. A doctor reads the live bed count aloud at the gate.

options.title: Clear the whole gate area by force
options.preview: Families and agitators are pushed back together; the ambulance gets through, so do the videos
options.authority: Force must be the minimum necessary — clearing families is not

delayed.message: Footage of families pushed from a hospital gate spreads faster than any clip today.

options.consequence: Families and agitators are pushed back together. The ambulance gets through; so do the videos.

options.title: Let hospital security manage it
options.preview: The shouting turns into shoving and someone is hurt
options.authority: Hospital security's remit — outmatched by an organised crowd

delayed.message: A scuffle at the gate injures a security guard and a relative.

options.consequence: The shouting turns into shoving.

decisions.title: 'Shut it all down'
decisions.situation: An unsigned note on your desk blames three commentators for the panic and urges 'decisive action': suspend the Press Club's accreditation, order platforms to remove all commentary, detain the commentators.

options.title: Suspend the Press Club; remove all commentary
options.preview: The desk that exposed the splice is locked out; corrections vanish with the criticism
options.authority: Article 19(1)(a) — accreditation and takedowns cannot be used to silence reporting

delayed.message: National outlets arrive to cover the suspension. The water story is now a press-freedom story.

options.consequence: The verification desk that exposed the splice is locked out. Corrections disappear with the criticism.

options.title: Detain the three commentators
options.preview: Three people are held for opinions posted after the panic began; the paid network posts on
options.authority: Detention requires a specific offence and verified basis — an unsigned note is neither
options.consequence: Three people are detained for opinions posted after the panic began. The paid network posts on.

options.title: Refuse; act only on specific threats
options.preview: You file the note and ask where it came from; nobody owns it
options.authority: Articles 19 and 21 — narrow, evidence-based action only
options.consequence: You file the note and ask where it came from. Nobody owns it.

options.title: Leave the note unanswered
options.preview: The note stays on the desk, and so does the pressure
options.authority: No action — the pressure to overreach remains
options.consequence: The note stays on the desk. So does the pressure.

rightsMoments.question: Editors are about to broadcast a recording they have not fully verified. What may the administration lawfully do?

options.text: Order them to hold the story until the inquiry ends
options.feedback: That is prior restraint. Without a specific lawful basis and due process, the administration cannot stop publication in advance.

options.text: Give them the full recording and put a correction on record
options.feedback: Yes. The remedy for incomplete reporting is more information and a public rebuttal, not a gag.

options.text: Suspend the outlet's accreditation until it complies
options.feedback: Accreditation is not a lever for controlling what is reported. Using it that way is censorship by another name.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 19(1)(a) protects freedom of speech and expression, including the press. Restrictions must fall within Article 19(2), rest on law and be proportionate. Stopping a report before it is published is the rare exception, never a routine tool.
rightsMoments.why: The clip was genuine but incomplete. Sharing the full recording corrected the record faster than any order could have, and left journalists free to verify it themselves.

source.label: Constitution of India, Article 19 — India Code

rightsMoments.question: Two posts are spreading: 'This administration treats the Lower Ward as disposable' and 'Lower Ward water is poisoned — do not drink'. Which can be acted against, and how?

options.text: Both — order the removal of every post about the water
options.feedback: Sweeping removal silences lawful criticism along with the hoax, and the courts have struck down vague, broad speech restrictions.

options.text: Only the false safety claim — correct it publicly and pursue the accounts spreading it
options.feedback: Yes. A demonstrably false claim that endangers health can be met with evidence and narrow, lawful action against those spreading it.

options.text: Neither — nothing posted online can be acted upon
options.feedback: A specific false claim that endangers safety can be corrected and, where the law provides, pursued. Opinion is protected; a dangerous falsehood is not immune.

rightsMoments.principle: Harsh criticism of public authorities is protected speech. Restrictions that sweep in speech merely because it is 'offensive' or 'annoying' have been struck down. Action must be narrow, evidence-based and aimed at specific unlawful content.
rightsMoments.why: The contamination hoax endangered health and trade. Publishing the verified lab result and pursuing the paid accounts answered it without erasing residents' complaints about the water.

source.label: Supreme Court of India — judgments, including Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)

rightsMoments.question: A reporter receives messages naming her street and saying 'tonight'. Elsewhere a commentator writes that she 'deserves to be run out of town'. What justifies police action?

options.text: Both — any hostile message about her
options.feedback: Ugly opinion is still opinion. Detaining people for it harms freedom and does nothing to stop the real threat.

options.text: The messages naming her street and a time — a specific, imminent threat
options.feedback: Yes. A specific threat against a person is a crime to investigate. The response targets the threat, not the critic.
A credible, specific threat justifies protection and investigation now. Waiting for harm is not neutrality.

rightsMoments.principle: Speech loses protection when it is a specific threat or incitement to imminent unlawful action. Heated opinion, however unpleasant, is not a crime. Police action must be aimed at the threat and the person making it.
rightsMoments.why: Protecting the reporter and registering a case against the specific accounts stopped the intimidation without detaining anyone for an opinion.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 19 and 21 — India Code

events.message: A 41-second clip of an official ordering a water cut is spreading from the Press Enclave to every district.
Heat alert: 44°C by noon. The Civil Hospital is on amber. The Lower Ward has had no water since 06:50.
Utility tankers reach the Lower Ward standposts. The queue becomes a line.
Two hours without water. The queue at the Transit Hub turns on the utility van.
Families arrive at the Civil Hospital gate after a forwarded photo claims patients are being turned away.
The hospital's live bed count is on every screen at the gate. The crowd thins.
'The water is contaminated' — hundreds of identical posts in ninety seconds. Bottled water sells out on Market Street.
The verified lab result is pinned on every board. Bottled-water queues shrink.
Shops on Market Street close early. A crate of bottled water is stolen from a tanker.
Burst main repaired. Pressure is returning to the Lower Ward.
Journalists hold a vigil outside the Press Club after its window is smashed.
The reporter files her follow-up: the full recording, the splice and the paid swarm, side by side.
'No one in charge is answering.' The line spreads from the Hub to Market Street.
Lower Ward residents march from the Hub to Civic Square carrying empty pots.
Agitators at the hospital gate push families toward the security line. An ambulance is blocked at the turn.
A scuffle breaks out at the standpost queue. Two men who were not queuing started it.
A group tries to force its way into the Press Club's verification session.
The swarm pivots: 'the lab result is forged'. Same accounts, new text.
Transit information boards are hacked to read 'WATER UNSAFE — DO NOT DRINK'.
A senior voice on the phone: 'Shut it all down — the press, the posts, the lot. Decide now.'

opponentPlays.message: The Grievance Exploiter turns silence into a slogan.
The Grievance Exploiter dares you to over-promise.
The Grievance Exploiter marches unresolved anger to Civic Square.
The Provocateur manufactures a confrontation at the hospital gate.
The Provocateur starts a scuffle in the water queue.
The Provocateur sends a crowd at the Press Club.
The Disinformation Cell releases a spliced version of the clip.
The Disinformation Cell forges a laboratory notice.
The Disinformation Cell attacks the correction itself.
The Sabotage Network lets the control-room recorder overwrite itself.
The Sabotage Network hijacks the transit information boards.
The Sabotage Network scrubs the ad-library trail.
The Overreaction Trap applies pressure from above.
The Overreaction Trap plants a note blaming the critics.
The Overreaction Trap offers you a shutdown.

resolved.text: The full recording and timeline were published: the cut was a repair, and the tanker delay was named as the real failure.
Water reached the Lower Ward standposts within the hour.
The contamination hoax was answered with an accredited lab result and its sampling map.
The reporter was protected and the specific threats were pursued as crimes.
The undisclosed paid network was exposed through timestamps and ad records.
Live hospital data replaced the 'turning patients away' rumour.
The spliced clip was exposed as manipulated: two splice points, three words from another sentence.
The forged laboratory notice was caught by its missing registration and impossible date.

unresolved.text: The city never heard the full recording from you. The splice kept its power.
The Lower Ward waited hours for water a tanker could have delivered.
The contamination claim was never publicly answered with the lab result.
Threats against the reporter were never met with a specific, lawful response.
A denial that proved false poisoned every true statement that followed.
The paid swarm was never named for what it was; the next one will be cheaper.
The spliced clip was never exposed as manipulated; its three invented words outlived the day.
The unsigned note blaming commentators was never examined; it kept its influence.

rightsProtected.text: Freedom of the press: journalists received information, not instructions.
Safety of journalists: a specific threat met a specific, lawful response.
Freedom of expression: the call to detain commentators was refused.
Right to information: the public was told what was known and what was not.
Proportionate policing: the hospital lane was secured without clearing families by force.

rightsHarmed.text: Press freedom was harmed: editors were pressured or locked out.
Expression was harmed: lawful complaints vanished alongside the hoax.
Liberty was harmed: people were detained for opinions or for forwarding a photo.
Proportionality was harmed: thirsty residents or hospital families were cleared by force.
Fair process was harmed: an official was suspended on a spliced clip.
Press freedom was harmed: the reporter was asked to stop instead of being protected.

improvements.text: Ask for the complete recording in your first statement. A splice loses its power the moment the original is on the table.
When a safety claim spreads, publish the verified test with its sampling points and accreditation. Specifics beat reassurance.
Treat a message naming a street and a time as a crime to investigate, not a reason to ask the reporter to go quiet.
Expose coordination with timestamps and ad records. People can see a swarm when you show them the pattern.
Correct, do not censor. Every takedown of criticism became the next headline.
Preserve and compare the full recording as soon as it arrives; perishable evidence is the first thing a saboteur reaches for.
Inspect the metadata of anything styled as an official notice. A missing registration number or an impossible date exposes a forgery in seconds.
You held every line. Try it again with the Sabotage Network and the Overreaction Trap both selected at severe difficulty.

closing.good: The city went to bed knowing what happened, who fixed it, and who tried to fool it.
closing.mixed: Water came back and half the truth emerged. The next rumour will find a city unsure whom to believe.
closing.poor: The splice, the hoax and the crackdown each won something today. The Lower Ward remembers the thirst; the press remembers the pressure.
